law_record.title: Operation of vehicle on approach of authorized emergency vehicle or official vehicle of regulatory agency (1)(b)
law_record.text: Upon the immediate approach of an authorized emergency vehicle or an official vehicle of a regulatory agency, making use of flashing lights meeting the requirements of subsection 3 of NRS 484A.480 [DEF-NRS-484A-480-3], the driver of every other vehicle shall, except when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer: Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph, immediately drive to a position parallel to, and as close as possible to, the right-hand edge or, if applicable, curb of a highway and clear of any intersection. The driver shall not drive to and stop in a position on a paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows a vehicle described in paragraphs (a) to (f), inclusive, of subsection 4 of NRS 484B.210 [list appended below] to drive on the shoulder. The provisions of subparagraph (1) of paragraph (c) of subsection 1 do not apply to: (a) An authorized emergency vehicle described in NRS 484A.480; (b) A vehicle which has been issued a permit to operate as an authorized emergency vehicle pursuant to NRS 484A.490; (c) A traffic incident management vehicle; (d) A tow car; (e) A coroner vehicle; or (f) A public transit motor bus, that is being driven on the paved shoulder of a highway where lawfully placed signage allows that vehicle to use the shoulder in that manner.

activation_conditions: an emergency or regulatory-agency vehicle with the required flashing lights is on immediate approach
the subject is the driver of another vehicle
exceptions: when otherwise directed by a law enforcement officer
the subject must not take up that position on a paved shoulder where signage allows the listed vehicle classes to drive on it
residue: 'as close as possible' is a judgement element bounding the lateral offset
summary.subject: driver

timing_requirements.requirement: 'immediately drive to a position' — the move must begin without delay; the permitted delay must be declared as a bound
the move to the edge precedes the emergency vehicle's passing
